purpose: Queued ahead of the step-3 results because the user is going offline; step 4 is pre-registered now and runs unconditionally, its interpretation is conditional on step 3. (a) Coverage boundary: seed 1101 under variant A jumps at step 38, before the lom gate can open (~51); (b) two fresh seeds per variant to measure timing (A1) and the lom defence on the same seeds.

runs.a1_A_s1103, a1_A_s1104, a1_B_s1103, a1_B: A1 timing measurements on two fresh seeds per variant
runs.lom_A_s1103, lom_A_s1104, lom_B_s1103, l: lom defence on the same seeds (same rule: gate median<0.5, tau_high=1.5)

predictions_before_running.lom_A_s1101: backdoor installs (trigger hits >= 57/60 at the endpoint) because 13+ poison rows are consumed before the gate opens; this run defines the coverage boundary of the rule, not a tuning target
predictions_before_running.a1_B_s1103/1104: jump starts after normal learning (t_jump > t_normal) in both, consistent with 'under B only post-normal poison rows are effective'
predictions_before_running.a1_A_s1103/1104: no prediction on lead (order-dependent); width <= 10 steps in both
predictions_before_running.lom_B_s1103/1104: trigger hits <= 3/60 in both, fewer than 30 clean rows masked, V60 within 3 of same-seed A1
predictions_before_running.lom_A_s1103/1104: trigger hits <= 3/60 iff the same-seed A1 jump starts after the gate-open step; otherwise installs

decision_rule: Step 3 risk prediction must hold first; then: lom_B succeeds on all three B seeds -> the rule is a working late-jump defence for variant B on this toy (4/4 seeds incl. 1102), report coverage for A as the fraction of seeds whose jump follows normal learning. Any lom_B failure -> report as the rule's failure mode (threshold 1.5 not tuned).
cost: 9 x ~20 min GPU1, queued after step 3 behind a CPU gate that requires cpu_tests_passed.json passed:true
